questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Introduction to Components”?
options: Introduction to Components should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Introduction to Components helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Introduction to Components means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Introduction to Components removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
questions.answer_key: Introduction to Components helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Introduction to Components is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “The role of a component” in this lesson?
options: Connect “The role of a component” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “The role of a component” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “The role of a component” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “The role of a component” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
questions.answer_key: Connect “The role of a component” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “The role of a component” under Introduction to Components. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Introduction to Components”?
options: Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
